scope_allowed: Relevance of the quantities of interest

models.name: Model A: Fully coupled ALE FSI with nonlinear contact
models.what_it_computes: Time-resolved axial drag, seal-zone contact pressure distribution, micro-slip per cycle, and onset of migration under pulsatile flow with compliant aortic wall and frictional stent–artery contact.

models.name: Model B: Partitioned FSI with reduced-order wall and surrogate contact
models.what_it_computes: Cycle-averaged axial force, effective seal pressure, and cumulative slip index using linearized wall dynamics and static contact surrogates driven by pulsatile boundary conditions.

mechanisms.name: Pulsatile axial drag
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Fluid momentum and pressure gradients impose an axial load that challenges seal friction and can initiate downstream migration.

mechanisms.name: Neck dilation under pressure
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Pressurization enlarges the aortic neck, reducing interference fit and contact pressure, thereby lowering migration resistance.

mechanisms.name: Curvature-induced proximal edge peeling
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Aortic curvature and device stiffness mismatch can lever the proximal edge, locally unloading the seal and promoting slip.

mechanisms.name: Respiratory-driven axial strain
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Cyclic longitudinal motion of the aorta modulates normal force and friction, potentially ratcheting the device distally over time.

deviation.detail: Model risk is reported as 7.2 on a 0–10 scale derived from weighted model influence and decision consequence.

expected_decision.outcome_source: Under the ASME V&V 40 lens, Model A attains higher credibility for estimating migration resistance across the four mechanisms, especially where local contact and transient coupling dominate.
rationale_keywords: robust agreement to targeted bench data

datasets: pressurization chamber for neck dilation under pressure
respiratory-driven axial strain linear actuator rig
requirements: a frictional capacity criterion with hysteresis: the product of the effective normal force and friction coefficient must exceed the envelope of applied axial loads for a specified number of cycles without accumulation of slip beyond a threshold (0.5 mm).
a pass/fail margin relative to a migration threshold derived from frictional capacity at the seal

name_keywords: slip per cycle and frictional work
cumulative slip index and frictional work

expected_context_of_use: In our context of use, model predictions inform design iterations and preclinical evaluations by quantifying a safety margin between applied axial loads and the frictional capacity provided by the seal.

spans: On a sequence of uniformly refined meshes, we observed second-order L2 convergence of the velocity field, with fine-grid errors of 0.13% in Model A and 0.21% in Model B at similar resolutions.
